entries.en: I don't fail missions.
Kaidan was a fine officer. He knew what the risks were, but he did what he had to.
Ash was a hell of a soldier. She knew what the risks were, but she did what she had to.
Things would have been a lot tougher if your men hadn't been with us, Captain.
I'll miss him.
I'll miss her.
The captain considers the mission a success. I defer to his judgment.
We lost a lot of people on Virmire. I hope it was worth it.
Thank you for your efforts, Commander. I'm sure you will be properly recognized.
You achieved a lot on Virmire. You have my respect.
You have my gratitude, Commander. Most people would have left our team behind.
Still, I find the the loss of Captain Kirrahe troubling. But I won't blame you. I know you lost one of your own, as well.
That does not console me. Our unit will feel the loss of the captain in ways that will be impossible to measure.
The mission was a success. That will have to be enough.
That is our lot, I suppose. But there may come a day when so many have been sacrificed, it will be impossible to tell who won.
You sacrificed much on Virmire. We have a kinship of loss.
Captain Kirrahe was a great man.
Lieutenant Alenko knew the risks. So did your captain.
He's just one man. Many more will be saved because of what he did.
It was a necessary loss.
We will not trouble you for long. Our unit will be disbanded as soon as we depart. Good luck, Commander Shepard.
Chief Williams knew the risks. So did your captain.
Captain Kirrahe will be missed. But many others will live because he gave his life.
Good luck, Commander Shepard.
Commander Shepard. We don't normally see you officer types down here in the engine room. What's the occasion?
She's the best ship I've ever served on. Probably the fastest vessel ever designed. And she's the only one using the new Tantalus drive core.
Proportionally, it's about twice the size of any other vessel. Not only are we faster, but we can run at FTL speeds longer before we have to discharge the core.
You can't hide a ship out in space. They emit too much heat and radiation. Too easy for sensors to pick them up. Unless you find a way to capture those emissions.
So our stealth systems trap the energy we give off in storage sinks built into the ship itself. No emissions to give away our location.
Eventually the sinks have to be vented. More than a few hours silent running and they overheat. Cook us inside our own hull.
A visual scan can still pick us up. Anyone looking out a window could see us as plain as day. But you have to be pretty close to get an actual visual out in space.
Most vessels rely on scanners. As long as the stealth systems are engaged, they can't see us. Not unless we accelerate to FTL speeds.
Cranking up to FTL blue-shifts our emissions, pushes them into frequencies too high to capture in the sinks. As soon as we make the jump, it's like setting off a flare.
Sensors can pick up our location whenever we enter or exit FTL flight. But for short range missions, our stealth systems are amazing. And we've got the only one.
If you name a class of Alliance ship, I've probably served on it. Everything from dreadnoughts and carriers right down to frigates like the Normandy.
My last assignment was on the Tokyo. Only a cruiser, but she was a good ship. Couldn't hold a candle to the Normandy, though.
I want to know more about the Normandy.
What's so special about the Tantalus drive core?
Fill me in on the IES stealth system. How does it work, exactly?
There's no way for anyone to detect us?
Why doesn't it work with faster than light travel?
Where else have you served, Adams?
Carry on, Adams.
Stealth system
Drive core?
So we're invisible?
FTL gives us away?
Shame about Jenkins, Commander.
Heard we're headed into the Terminus Systems, Commander.
Don't worry, ma'am. The Normandy's a hell of a ship. She'll get us through this.
Don't worry, sir. The Normandy's a hell of a ship. She'll get us through this.
Hey, Commander. You know that quarian? Tali? She's been spending all her time down here asking me about our engines.
What? No! She's amazing! I wish my guys were half as smart as she is. Give her a month on board and she'll know more about our engines than I do!
She's got a real knack for technology, that one. I can see why you wanted her to come along.
You've got an eye for talent, Commander. But I'm guessing that's not why you came down here.
Normally I don't have anything nice to say about politicians, but he made a good call on this. But I'm guessing that's not why you came down here.
I'll tell her to leave you alone.
I figured she'd be a real asset to the team.
Ambassador Udina made me take her along.
I'll talk to her.
I'll get rid of her.
Is she bothering you?
She's useful.
I didn't.
We're fugitives on the run. Very exciting, Shepard.
Your ship's amazing, Shepard. I've never seen a drive core like this before. I can't believe you were able to fit it into a ship this small.
Oh. Hello, Shepard.
Shepard. I'm glad you're here.
It feels like we're getting near the end, doesn't it, Shepard? With Saren, I mean.
Hey, Shepard. You need something?
I could get used to living like this.
I love this place -- the crowds, the action. It's great!
Why would anyone want to live here?
If my people found an uninhabited world like this, they'd just keep on looking.
I've never seen snow before. Can't say I'm impressed.
I don't like it here. Too muggy.
This place gives me the creeps.
Saren's got to be close now!
I'm here, Shepard.
With you all the way.
I want to know more about the Pilgrimage.
Tell me about your people.
I want to know more about the geth.
Pilgrimage
I wonder what the Council would do to us if we got caught?
See you later.
I'm starting to understand why you humans have been so successful. I had no idea Alliance vessels were so advanced!
A month ago, I was patching a makeshift fuel line into a converted tug ship in the flotilla. Now I'm sitting on board one of the most advanced vessels in Citadel space.
I have to thank you again for bringing me along. Traveling on a vessel like this is a dream come true for me.
We're on the same side here. My people have more reason to hate the geth than anyone, remember?
But you can't blame me for being a little excited. I never dreamed I'd get a chance to travel on a ship as advanced as the Normandy.
It comes with being a quarian. The Migrant Fleet is the key to the survival of my people. Ships are our most valuable resource.
But we don't have anything like this. We make do with cast-offs and second-hand equipment. We just try to keep them running for as long as we can.
Some of the Fleet's larger vessels date all the way back to our original flight from the geth.
They're constantly being repaired, modified, and refitted. They aren't pretty, but they work. Mostly.
We've tried to make ourselves as independent as possible on the flotilla. Grow our own food, mine and process our own fuel.
But some things we just can't make on our own. A patch to maintain the hull integrity requires raw materials we just don't have. That's why our Pilgrimages are so important.
No problem. What do you want to talk about?
I know why I'm here. I'll do whatever I can to help you stop Saren and drive his geth armies back beyond the Veil.
Never mind. It's nothing. I'll be fine.
I don't know. Your ship is amazing, and your crew's been really great to me. Especially your chief engineer. But I just sort of feel... out of place.
The Normandy runs so smooth it feels like we're not even moving. And the engines are so quiet. How do you sleep at night?
Back on the flotilla, the last thing you want to hear is silence. It means an engine's died or an air filter's shut down.
I guess you don't have to worry about that here, but old habits die hard.
But it's more than just the silence. This ship feels so empty; it's like half the crew is missing.
Back home, I couldn't wait to go on my Pilgrimage. I couldn't wait to get away from the crowds. Now that I'm out here, I kind of miss them.
Don't worry. Like I said, it's nothing. I'll be there when you need me.
The Normandy's a prototype. Cutting edge technology.
I don't like the idea of aliens studying the architecture of Alliance ships.
I had no idea you found ship technology so interesting.
I can't believe your fleet's still using ships that are three centuries old.
I didn't bring you along to admire my ship.
What's your problem?
I didn't mean to snap at you. What's wrong?
The silence wakes you up?
I find it rather peaceful. Don't worry, you'll get used to it.
You'll get used to it.
Sometimes we don't appreciate what we have until it's gone.
I don't have time to deal with your personal problems.
This ship's special.
Normally they're not.
Gathering information on us?
You're into ships?
That's not why you're here.
That was 300 years ago.
You sound down.
Like I need this.
It's too quiet to sleep?
I like the silence.
It's not so bad.
I manage.
You're homesick.
Don't worry, Shepard. I know what's at stake. If we don't stop Saren, I won't have a home to go back to. I'll be ready when you need me.
Sounds like the Pilgrimage isn't just about finding resources for the fleet. Maybe it's about teaching you to appreciate your people and culture.
I need my crew to be in top form. I can't have you daydreaming about going home.
Maybe that's the point.
Stay focused.
Checking up on me, Shepard? Don't worry; I'm still here. But as soon as we stop Saren, I'm gone. My Pilgrimage can't wait forever.
Shepard, I need to talk to you. It's important.
You know the data you took from those geth control nodes? The information you uploaded to Alliance control? I want a copy of it.
Please! You don't understand what this could mean to my people!
Those files have information that could be vital to our efforts to understand the geth. It could be the key to helping us reclaim our homeworld!
Not right away. I'll stay with you as long as it takes to stop Saren. But my people need this!
Not right away. We will need to study it. It could take years. But it will give us new insight into how the geth have changed and evolved over the past centuries.
My people--I--owe you a great debt. One I can never repay.
The only thing I can offer in return is what you already have: my solemn promise to stay with you until Saren and his geth armies are defeated.
Thank you, Shepard.
Maybe even decades. But it's worth the time. This information will give us new insight into how the geth have changed and evolved over the past centuries.
Right. I'm sure the Alliance will have no problem turning it over to my people. Governments are always eager to work with the Migrant Fleet.
You're looking out for your own people. I understand that. I just wish it wasn't at my people's expense.
